title: 幻想水滸伝II

layouts.notes: 0x8002590C points to the dialogue window while there is one, else 0; the game allocates it, so its address changes. In it: 0x64 points to the text, 4 rows of 23 16-bit cells filled as the line is typed; 0x80 points to the speaker's name; byte 0x21 is 0 while typing, 2 while waiting for a press; bytes 0x0A and 0x0B are the typing column and row. Answers to a question come as the message, one a row, with the hero as speaker; no flag for them was found. Notices in their own small window (someone joins the party) are not read. A window of another size than 23 by 4 would be misread; none was seen.

sources: Headless replay from power-on: the opening scene's dialogue, its first choice, the party notice, walking, and talking to a soldier outside; about 100 frames compared with the layout's reading

The game's font in video memory, matched glyph by glyph against the first game's table (SLPS-00097); the other glyphs read from the dialogue on the disc, which is in plain codes, and against a reference 12-pixel font
notes: One 16-bit table for the whole game (tables/ps1/SLPM-86168.tbl): the code is the glyph's place in the font. The dialogue is on the disc in plain codes (kana one byte, kanji two with a lead byte 01-03, 8 above the table's code) under CDROM/, so a scan in a standard encoding finds nothing. Not reached in the replay: towns, shops, battles, the war and duel screens. Window frame pieces, cursor marks and item icons (0x00-0x0F, 0x38-0x3B, 0xF2-0xF7) are not mapped.
